title: WM-MT146-MergeReviewGuiFlow
clause: Operator merge-review flow: native egui pane + SessionWorkbench extension (pending list, SideBySide diff preview, conflict->merge-UI, approve/execute/abort); AccessKit + Argus evidence

scope.summary:
GOAL: Ship the OPERATOR-facing merge-review flow that mounts the MT-142 engine, MT-143 conflict bridge, and MT-145 governance gate behind a real surface: a native egui merge-review pane in handshake_native and a matching SessionWorkbench (React) extension, so an operator can see pending session-branch merges, preview each diff, open conflicts in the existing 3-pane merge UI, and approve / execute / abort — with the protected-branch consent gate (MT-145) enforced in the UI. This is the family's single GUI MT (MT-141..145 are backend/logic; MT-147 reclaim, MT-148 proofs).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) Native: NEW pane module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/merge_review_panel.rs (registered in code_editor/mod.rs) rendering the pending-merge list + diff preview + action bar; it REUSES DiffEditorPanel SideBySide for read-only diff preview and mounts the MT-143 merge_conflict_bridge for conflict resolution — it rebuilds neither. (b) React: extend app/src/components/swarm/SessionWorkbench.tsx (and a NEW app/src/components/swarm/MergeReviewPanel.tsx sub-component) following SessionWorkbench's established pattern of composing existing surfaces via injected callbacks and adding the MINIMUM IPC needed to list/preview/approve/execute/abort merges. (c) Backend IPC: a thin command surface exposing MT-145 governance (list pending, fetch diff/conflicts, submit approval grant, execute, abort). (d) Headless AccessKit tests + Argus visual evidence both sides.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Native pane (merge_review_panel.rs):
   - PendingMergeList: one row per proposed merge (merge_intent_id, source session/branch, target branch, protected? badge, MT-run validation verdict badge, state: Proposed|Approved|Conflicted|Executed|Aborted|Blocked). Data comes from the MT-145 audit/state surface; the pane NEVER fabricates a merge.
   - Diff preview: selecting a row shows a READ-ONLY DiffEditorPanel in DiffMode::SideBySide (existing constructor `DiffEditorPanel::side_by_side`, diff_editor_panel.rs ~255) of target vs merged-result (or per-file diffs); no editing in preview.
   - Conflict list: when state is Conflicted, list conflicted paths; 'Open in merge UI' mounts the MT-143 merge_conflict_bridge -> DiffEditorPanel DiffMode::Merge (3 panes local/base/remote) for that path. Resolution flows through the SAME bridge API; the pane adds no auto-resolution.
   - Action bar: Approve (only shown/enabled for a protected target awaiting consent; submits a MergeApprovalGrant via IPC), Execute (runs the governed merge; disabled while unresolved conflicts remain or validation is Unsatisfied without override), Abort (always available while a merge is in Proposed/Conflicted state; drives MergeSession::abort). Result state (CleanMerged commit id, Conflicts count, Blocked reason) is shown honestly.
   - Stable AccessKit author_ids (MT-contract identifiers, same discipline as diff_editor_panel.rs's diff_mode_toggle const ~line 54): merge_review.pending_list, merge_review.row.<merge_intent_id>, merge_review.diff_preview, merge_review.conflict_list, merge_review.action.approve, merge_review.action.execute, merge_review.action.abort.
2. React (SessionWorkbench.tsx + MergeReviewPanel.tsx):
   - Mirror the native surface for the operator board: pending merges list, diff/conflict summary, and approve/execute/abort actions bound to the new IPC. Follow the SessionWorkbench contract exactly — compose, do not rebuild; honest-disable any action whose IPC callback is absent (the pattern already used for onShowTerminal/onReviewSession/onResumeSession); add NO duplicate merge logic in TS.
   - The React panel shows the protected-branch badge and requires an explicit operator confirm before submitting an approval grant (consent is a deliberate two-step, never a single accidental click).
3. Backend IPC (Tauri command surface, app/src or src-tauri bridge): list_pending_merges, get_merge_preview(merge_intent_id), get_merge_conflicts(merge_intent_id), submit_merge_approval(grant), execute_merge(merge_intent_id), abort_merge(merge_intent_id). Each maps to the MT-145 governance gate + MT-142/143 engine; NONE bypasses the gate. Approvals carry the operator id so the MT-145 audit row records who approved.
4. HARD RULES: the UI cannot bypass the MT-145 consent gate (Execute on a protected target with no grant returns Blocked and the pane shows it); no auto-resolution surfaced (conflicts always route to the MT-143 3-pane UI); no force / no push control exists anywhere in the surface; the pane must be QUIET (HBR-QUIET) — no focus stealing / no foreground popups while models or other operators work; git code-merge vs CRDT document-merge boundary holds (this surface never edits CRDT documents).
5. BOUNDARY: reuse DiffEditorPanel (SideBySide + Merge) and merge_conflict_bridge as-is; this MT wires them into a review flow and adds the pending-list + action-bar + IPC. It does not modify the merge engine, the conflict bridge internals, or the governance policy.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read diff_editor_panel.rs (DiffMode SideBySide/Inline/Merge ~73-95, DiffEditorPanel::side_by_side ~255, DiffEditorPanel::merge ~305, AccessKit author_id const ~54) and the existing headless egui_kittest/AccessKit diff-panel tests; read merge_conflict_bridge.rs (MT-143) and SessionWorkbench.tsx (composition + honest-disable pattern).
2. Implement merge_review_panel.rs: pending list, SideBySide diff preview, conflict list, action bar, with the stable author_ids above; mount merge_conflict_bridge for conflict rows.
3. Add the Tauri IPC commands mapping to MT-145/142/143; ensure every path goes through the governance gate (no direct engine call that skips it).
4. Implement MergeReviewPanel.tsx and wire it into SessionWorkbench.tsx via injected callbacks with honest-disable; add the two-step protected-approval confirm.
5. Native headless tests (egui_kittest/AccessKit): pending list renders rows from a fixture; SideBySide preview populates; a Conflicted row opens the 3-pane merge UI; Approve is enabled only for a protected-awaiting-consent row; Execute is disabled while unresolved conflicts remain; Abort is available in Proposed/Conflicted.
6. React tests (component/RTL): list + actions render; actions honest-disable when callbacks absent; protected approval requires the confirm step.
7. Argus visual evidence: capture the pending list, the SideBySide preview, the 3-pane merge open, and each action state (approve-enabled / execute-blocked / result) for both surfaces; record targets for a no-context model to reproduce.
8. Run proof targets; record measured output + Argus artifact paths.

src-tauri/**/merge* (Tauri command surface for the governed merge flow, if the IPC layer lives here)

acceptance_criteria: A native egui merge-review pane (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/merge_review_panel.rs) renders a pending-merge list, a read-only SideBySide diff preview (reusing DiffEditorPanel::side_by_side), a conflict list, and an Approve/Execute/Abort action bar.
Conflicted merges open in the EXISTING 3-pane merge UI via the MT-143 merge_conflict_bridge (DiffMode::Merge); the pane adds no second merge view and no auto-resolution.
SessionWorkbench.tsx is extended with a MergeReviewPanel that mirrors the flow following the compose + honest-disable pattern; absent IPC callbacks disable actions honestly rather than faking them.

Every UI action routes through the MT-145 governance gate: Execute on a protected target with no operator approval is Blocked and the pane shows the Blocked reason; approval is a deliberate two-step operator confirm.

Stable AccessKit author_ids exist for pending_list, each row, diff_preview, conflict_list, and the approve/execute/abort actions; headless AccessKit tests assert their presence and enabled/disabled state transitions.
Abort is available while a merge is Proposed/Conflicted and drives MergeSession::abort; a test proves an aborted merge leaves no MERGE_HEAD (delegated to the MT-142 guarantee).
No force / no push control exists in the surface (grep-provable: no push/force affordance in the new pane, panel, or IPC files).

Argus visual evidence is captured for the pending list, SideBySide preview, 3-pane merge open, and action states (approve-enabled / execute-blocked / result) on both native and React surfaces, with reproduction targets recorded.
The pane is QUIET: no foreground window pop, focus steal, or input hijack during model/operator work (HBR-QUIET), verified in the headless run.
proof_targets: bash -lc "cd app && npm test -- MergeReviewPanel 2>&1 | tail -40"
code_surfaces: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/merge_review_panel.rs (NEW pane: pending list, SideBySide preview, conflict list, action bar, AccessKit author_ids)
app/src/components/swarm/SessionWorkbench.tsx (EXTEND: compose merge-review via injected callbacks; honest-disable ~35-61)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge_policy.rs (READ-ONLY: MT-145 governance the IPC maps to)
expected_tests: native headless (egui_kittest/AccessKit): pending list renders fixture rows with protected/validation badges
native headless: selecting a row populates the SideBySide preview; a Conflicted row opens the 3-pane merge UI via the bridge
native headless: Approve enabled only for protected-awaiting-consent; Execute disabled while unresolved conflicts remain; Abort available in Proposed/Conflicted
native headless: Execute on a protected target with no grant surfaces the MT-145 Blocked reason (no merge)
React (RTL): panel renders; actions honest-disable when callbacks absent; protected approval requires the two-step confirm
Argus: visual snapshots of pending list, preview, 3-pane merge, and action states captured on both surfaces
implementation_notes: Reuse is mandatory: DiffEditorPanel SideBySide is the preview and DiffEditorPanel Merge (via the MT-143 bridge) is the conflict UI; building any new diff/merge view is rejected (MT-143 already made this decision for the merge view).

Follow SessionWorkbench's contract literally (SessionWorkbench.tsx ~4-61): compose existing surfaces via injected callbacks, add no redundant IPC, honest-disable when a callback is absent — do not fabricate a merge or a conflict.
Consent is a two-step UI action on protected targets: the approval click plus an explicit confirm, so an accidental single click cannot approve a merge into main.
IPC must never expose an execute path that skips the MT-145 gate; the only merge execution route is the governed one, so the pane physically cannot force or bypass a protected merge.

Argus is the required visual-debug evidence surface (GLOBAL-BUILD visual debugging): capture readable/discoverable/non-overlapping states for a no-context model; record the exact targets and reproduction steps.
Keep the native pane free of shell/pane-registry assumptions beyond what code_editor/mod.rs registration needs, so the host surface mounts it without rework.
Merge-review annotations (comments on resolved files) are the later MT-201+ annotations family; do not build annotation storage in this pane.

surfaces: Native egui merge-review pane (merge_review_panel.rs): pending-merge list, read-only SideBySide diff preview, conflict list, Approve/Execute/Abort action bar
React SessionWorkbench merge-review extension (MergeReviewPanel.tsx): pending list, diff/conflict summary, approve/execute/abort with two-step protected-approval confirm
argus_targets: merge_review.pending_list (rows with protected + MT-run validation badges)
merge_review.action.approve (enabled state on a protected-awaiting-consent row)
merge_review.action.execute (blocked state while conflicts unresolved / no approval)
merge_review.result_state (CleanMerged commit id / Conflicts count / Blocked reason)

target_entries: Source Control > Merge review (pending merges, diff preview, opening conflicts in the 3-pane merge UI)
Source Control > Approving a protected merge (two-step operator consent; what the protected badge means)
Source Control > Executing/aborting a merge from the review pane (blocked states and how to clear them)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Operator approve/execute/abort actions flow through the MT-145 governance gate, which writes the MergeAuditRow + MT-161 merge FR events; the pane surfaces the resulting lifecycle state, so operator-driven transitions are recorded.
Emit a diagnostic event on an IPC command failure (list/preview/execute) surfaced to the pane, via the open diagnostic-event API if present; else DEFERRED-with-reason.

The review pane runs inside the long-lived native/React app; UI liveness is covered by the app-level watchers (Argus + existing app health), not a per-pane capture — record WIRED-via-app or DEFERRED-with-reason accordingly.

risk_if_missed: The whole merge-back family stays headless: operators cannot see pending session merges, cannot preview or resolve conflicts in-app, and cannot exercise the MT-145 consent gate — they drop to raw git (unaudited, bypassing protection), and MT-148 has no operator surface to prove.

risks: RISK-1: The UI exposes an execute path that bypasses the MT-145 consent gate (a direct engine IPC), letting an operator merge into a protected branch with no recorded approval.
RISK-2: A single accidental click approves a protected merge (no confirm step), or the protected badge is missing, so the operator does not realize consent is being granted for main/release.
RISK-3: The pane rebuilds a merge/diff view instead of reusing DiffEditorPanel, diverging from the real resolution logic so what the operator resolves is not what gets committed.
RISK-4: A force-push or push affordance leaks into the surface (a 'publish'/'sync' button), reintroducing the exact capability the family forbids.
RISK-5: The pane pops a foreground window / steals focus during model or parallel-operator work (HBR-QUIET violation), disrupting the swarm.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): The only merge-execution IPC is the governed one; a test asserts execute_merge on a protected target with no grant returns Blocked and no merge commit exists, and there is no non-governed engine command exposed to the UI.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Approval is a deliberate two-step (click + confirm) with a visible protected badge; AccessKit/RTL tests assert the confirm is required and the badge renders for protected targets.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Preview reuses DiffEditorPanel::side_by_side and conflicts reuse the MT-143 bridge -> DiffEditorPanel::merge; forbidden_paths block editing those files, and an end-to-end test proves the resolved buffer the UI produces is the buffer committed (shared with MT-148).
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): grep proof target asserts no push/force affordance in the pane/panel/IPC files; the surface offers approve/execute/abort only.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Headless run asserts no foreground/focus-steal side effect; the pane renders in-surface and background-quiet per HBR-QUIET.

research_provenance.source: Verified current code: wtc-native-editors-v1 src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs — DiffMode { SideBySide, Inline, Merge } lines 73-95, DiffEditorPanel::side_by_side ~255, DiffEditorPanel::merge ~305 (3 panes local/base/remote), stable AccessKit author_id const ~54 (diff_mode_toggle) with an existing egui_kittest/AccessKit headless test discipline; app/src/components/swarm/SessionWorkbench.tsx lines 4-61 (compose existing surfaces via injected callbacks, add NO new IPC beyond need, honest-disable when a callback is absent). MT-142 engine, MT-143 merge_conflict_bridge, and MT-145 governance gate are the backend this pane mounts. Field practice: the pending-list + diff-preview + resolve + approve/merge flow mirrors GitHub/GitLab merge-request review and Vibe-Kanban-style operator panels, reusing the in-app 3-pane mergetool contract instead of an external tool.
corrections: Reuse decisions baked in: DiffEditorPanel SideBySide is the preview; the MT-143 bridge -> DiffEditorPanel Merge is the conflict UI; SessionWorkbench's compose + honest-disable contract is followed — no rebuilt views, no fabricated merges.

Operator/red-team hard rules: protected merges require a two-step operator consent enforced by the MT-145 gate (the UI cannot bypass it); no force / no push affordance; no auto-resolution; QUIET (no focus steal) per HBR-QUIET.
Git code-merge vs CRDT document-merge boundary restated; the review surface never edits CRDT documents. Merge-review annotations deferred to the MT-201+ annotations family.
